shape.text: An organization access token is the prefix polar_oat_ followed by exactly 43 letters and digits, 53 characters in all. The provider's server code adds the prefix, and its token generator fixes the body length.

The body is 37 random letters and digits followed by a 6-character checksum: the CRC32 of the 37 characters written in base62 (digit order 0-9, A-Z, a-z) and zero-padded. The service that issues these tokens postdates the introduction of the checksum, so there is only one era.
A failed checksum does not by itself show that a value is not a token.

unresolved.reason: The treatment of a failed checksum is a project choice, not a provider statement: a shape-valid value with a mismatching checksum is still treated as a token.

issuance.text: The token is read from POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN and sent as Authorization: Bearer; the Python and JavaScript SDKs take it as access_token or accessToken.
No Polar organization access token was issued or observed for this record.

unresolved.reason: No token was issued; the grammar rests on the provider's server code.

collisions.text: Polar webhook secrets are whsec_ followed by 43 characters from the same generator. The whsec_ prefix is already used for Stripe webhook signing secrets, so it does not identify a Polar credential.

polar_ci_ is a public OAuth client identifier and polar_c_ and polar_cl_ checkout client secrets are handed to the browser by design; session, authorization-code and verification tokens are short-lived.
